282-program-description: Inequality, governance, conflict, environment and development themes, with training in research methods.
282-course-selection-guidelines-for-the-: At least 18 of 36 credits at 300+, at least 9 INTD, at most 12 in any other discipline. Some Field Studies courses can count.
283-sociology: Choose Methods courses with the IDS Adviser, and check Arts' course overlap policy.
286-program-description: The same themes in depth, with research methods. Keep 3.50 in program courses and CGPA 3.00.
290-course-selection-guidelines-for-the-: At least 18 of 36 at 300+, 9 at 400+, 12 INTD, at most 12 in another discipline. Some Field Studies courses can count.
Econ-IDS students take ECON 257D, so not ECON 227D.
290-methods-6-credits: Choose with the IDS Adviser, and check the overlap policy.
294-about-jewish-studies: Interdisciplinary Judaica since 1968. Courses for all students, Hebrew, Yiddish and Aramaic at all levels, specialized courses, a minor, a major, and an honours program preparing you for graduate work.
294-jewish-studies-related-program-jewis: Since 1973, with Education, it prepares elementary and secondary teachers. Build a foundation in Bible, liturgy, traditions and history first; those weak in Hebrew are encouraged to spend a term at an Israeli university. Director: Dr. Eric Caplan.
294-location: Leacock Building, 855 Sherbrooke St. W., 7th floor.
294-program-description: All courses are complementary for flexibility, with no language requirement. Can expand to the Major.
294-areas-of-jewish-studies: At least 9 normally at an advanced level in one area, such as Biblical, East European, History, Thought, Literature, Modern or Rabbinic.
296-other-department-courses-history: These History courses count, and related courses elsewhere, such as Classical Greek, Arabic or literary theory, may be encouraged.
296-program-description: All courses are complementary for flexibility.
296-jewish-language: 6 credits showing advanced Hebrew or Yiddish.
296-areas-of-jewish-studies: 24 credits, at least 12 in one area. Without the language background, substitute up to 12 language credits. Language courses are under Language and Literature.
298-program-requirements: Keep program GPA and CGPA at 3.00.
299-jewish-language: 0–18 credits, reaching advanced level in at least one Jewish language. If you can show competence, you may substitute other courses.
299-areas-of-jewish-studies: 27–45 credits reaching advanced level in two areas, chosen with an adviser.
